title: KU establishes research partnership with Kansas-based AI and cybersecurity company
summary_en: The University of Kansas has established a research partnership with SOFTwarfare, a Kansas-based AI operations and cybersecurity technology company, to explore opportunities in cybersecurity, trusted computing and artificial intelligence.
title_cn: KU establishes research partnership with Kansas-based AI and cybersecurity company

title: KU students present plans to promote local news in Media Innovation Challenge
summary_en: Three teams of undergraduate students presented ideas Nov. 12 to increase revenue at rural newspapers during the journalism school’s inaugural Media Innovation Challenge. Each pitch was presented in front of a panel of five industry and faculty judges for a “Shark Tank”-style competition, with the audience serving as a collective sixth judge.
title_cn: KU students present plans to promote local news in Media Innovation Challenge

title: 15 Jayhawks named to 2027 Global Scholars cohort
summary_en: The University of Kansas 2027 Global Scholars will pursue internationally focused research with faculty mentors, with opportunities to study and conduct research abroad before presenting their work as seniors.
title_cn: 15 Jayhawks named to 2027 Global Scholars cohort

title: Babies rarely see exaggerated facial expressions used in emotion research, study shows
summary_en: A new paper in Communications Psychology calls into question the value of exaggerated facial expressions commonly used in research to study babies’ emotional understanding. The study, led by University of Kansas researchers, shows that babies ages 6-17 months rarely encounter these expressions in everyday life — and rarely see full faces at all.
title_cn: Babies rarely see exaggerated facial expressions used in emotion research, study shows

title: New protocol finds ways to relieve overcrowding at hospital emergency departments, study finds
summary_en: In a new article, Suman Mallik, B. Allen and Dorothy V. Lay Professor at the University of Kansas School of Business, examines the efficiency of the full-capacity protocol (FCP), a set of temporary hospital-wide guidelines designed to alleviate crowding at the emergency department.
title_cn: New protocol finds ways to relieve overcrowding at hospital emergency departments, study finds
